source.title: AUTOMORPHISMS AND DYNAMICS: A LIST OF OPEN PROBLEMS

accepted.question_text: Let n ≥ 2. Which subgroups Γ of GL_n(Z) can occur as the discrete automorphism group of a projective variety? More precisely: when is Γ abstractly realizable, meaning that there exists a projective variety X whose automorphism group Aut(X) is isomorphic to Γ as an abstract group; and when is Γ strongly realizable, meaning that there exists a smooth complex projective variety X and a Z-defined linear algebraic representation φ: GL_m(R) → GL(H^2(X; R)) such that the discrete cohomological action Aut(X)^* coincides with φ(Γ)? In particular, is every finitely generated subgroup Γ ⊂ GL_n(Z) abstractly realizable, or strongly realizable, as a group of automorphisms?
accepted.context_brief: Realizability of linear groups as automorphism groups

evidence.quote: Question 2.5. Which subgroups of GLn(Z) are abstractly (resp. strongly) realizable as groups of automorphisms ? Is every finitely generated subgroup Γ ⊂ GLn(Z) abstractly (resp. strongly) realizable as a group of automorphisms ?

say that a group Γ is abstractly realizable as a group of automorphisms (in dimension d) if there exist a projective variety X (of dimension d) such that Aut(X) is isomorphic to Γ (as abstract groups).

Say that a group Γ ⊂ GLm(Z) is strongly realizable as a group of automorphisms if there is a smooth complex projective variety X, and a linear algebraic representation ϕ: GLm(R) → GL(H2(X; R)) which is defined over Z, such that Aut(X)∗ coincides with ϕ(Γ).

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a rational surface S whose automorphism group Aut(S) is discrete but not finitely generated? More specifically, can one construct such a rational surface S so that the pair (S, Aut(S)) is minimal in the sense that whenever π: S → S' is a birational morphism with π ∘ Aut(S) ∘ π^{-1} contained in Aut(S'), the morphism π must already be an isomorphism?
accepted.context_brief: Non-finitely generated automorphism groups of rational surfaces

evidence.quote: Remark 2.6. The following problem remains open: does there exist a rational surface S such that Aut(S) is discrete but not finitely generated ? More precisely, can one find such an example which is a minimal model for the pair (S, Aut(S)), meaning that if π : S → S' is a birational morphism and π ◦ Aut(S) ◦ π−1 ⊂ Aut(S') then π is an isomorphism ?

accepted.question_text: Fix an integer d ≥ 2. For a Calabi–Yau variety X of dimension d, let G^0(X) denote the neutral component of the Zariski closure of the discrete cohomological action Aut(X)^* inside GL(H^2(X; R)). Which linear algebraic groups can occur as G^0(X) when X ranges over all Calabi–Yau varieties of dimension d?
accepted.context_brief: Zariski closures of automorphism actions on Calabi–Yau varieties

evidence.quote: Question 2.7. Fix a dimension d ≥ 2. Define G0(X) as the neutral component of the Zariski closure of Aut(X)∗ in GL(H2(X; R)). What kind of linear algebraic groups G0(X) do we obtain in this way, when X runs over all possible Calabi-Yau varieties of dimension d ?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a real projective K3 surface X such that the real locus X(R) is connected of genus g ≥ 2 and the mapping-class homomorphism α_{X(R)}: Aut(X_R) → Mod(X(R)) is surjective?
accepted.context_brief: Mapping classes realized by automorphisms of real K3 surfaces

evidence.quote: Question 2.8. Does there exist a real projective K3 surface X such that (i) X(R) is connected and of genus g ≥ 2 and (ii) the image of αX(R) : Aut(XR) → Mod(X(R)) is surjective ?

accepted.question_text: For dimension 3, let S_1(3) be the set of first dynamical degrees λ_1(f) arising from automorphisms f of smooth projective threefolds. Is S_1(3) dense in [1, ∞), or is there instead an ε > 0 such that S_1(3) contains no element in the interval (1, 1 + ε]?
accepted.context_brief: Distribution of first dynamical degrees in dimension three

evidence.quote: Now, fix the dimension d of the variety, and define the following set of real integers: S1(d) = {λ1(f); f ∈ Aut(X) for X smooth, projective, of dimension d}.
Question 2.9. Is S1(3) dense in [1, +∞[ ? Or, on the contrary, does there exist ε > 0 such that S1(3)∩]1, 1 + ε] is empty ?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a smooth complex projective variety of dimension 3, and let f be an automorphism of X whose induced linear action f^* on H^*(X; C) is non-trivial and unipotent. Must there exist a non-trivial meromorphic fibration π: X ⇢ B, meaning a dominant rational map with 0 < dim(B) < dim(X), such that f permutes the fibers of π; equivalently, such that there is a birational transformation f_B of B with π ∘ f = f_B ∘ π?
accepted.context_brief: Unipotent automorphisms and invariant fibrations in dimension three

evidence.quote: Question 3.1. Let X be a smooth complex projective variety of dimension 3. Let f be an automorphism of X, such that the linear transformation f∗ ∈ GL(H∗(X; C)) is non-trivial and unipotent. Does f permute the fibers of a non-trivial meromorphic fibration π : X 99K B ?

By “non-trivial meromorphic fibration”, I mean that 0 < dim(B) < dim(X) and π is a dominant rational map; and f permutes the fibers of π if there is a birational transformation fB of B such that π ◦ f = fB ◦ π.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a Calabi–Yau threefold and let f be an automorphism of X whose action on cohomology is non-trivial and unipotent. If κ is a Kähler form on X with cohomology class [κ] ∈ H^2(X; R), then n^{-k}(f^n)^*[κ] converges to an f-invariant nef class. Is this limiting f-invariant nef class induced by, or otherwise directly related to, an f-invariant fibration on X?
accepted.context_brief: Invariant nef classes and fibrations on Calabi–Yau threefolds

evidence.quote: So, let f be an automorphism of a Calabi-Yau variety X of dimension 3, with a non-trivial unipotent action on the cohomology. Consider a kähler form κ on X, with cohomology class [κ] ∈ H2(X; R); then n−k(f n)∗[κ] converges towards an f-invariant nef class. Is this class related to an f-invariant fibration on X ?

accepted.question_text: Let X be a smooth projective variety of dimension d with polarization H, and let f be a birational transformation of X whose first dynamical degree satisfies λ_1(f) = 1, equivalently so that the degrees deg_H(f^n) do not grow exponentially fast. Must the sequence deg_H(f^n) grow polynomially in n? If the sequence is unbounded, must it at least grow linearly? In particular, can one construct a birational transformation, for example of P^3_C, whose degree growth behaves like exp(√n), or like n^2 log n, or like n^(1/3)?
accepted.context_brief: Degree growth when the first dynamical degree equals one

evidence.quote: Instead of assuming that the entropy of f is zero, one may now assume that λ1(f) = 1, i.e. that degH(f n) does not grow exponentially fast with n.

Question 3.2. Let X be a smooth projective variety of dimension d, together with a polarization H. Let f be a birational transformation of X with λ1(f) = 1. Does the sequence degH(f n) grow polynomially ? If not bounded, does this sequence grow at least linearly ?
In other words, can one construct a birational transformation f, say, of P3 C, such that the sequence degH(f n) grows like exp(√n), or like n2 log(n), or like n1/3 ?

accepted.question_text: Let f be a birational transformation of a complex projective variety X with first dynamical degree λ_1(f) = 1. Does this condition force the existence of a non-trivial invariant fibration, meaning a dominant rational map π: X ⇢ B with 0 < dim(B) < dim(X) and a birational transformation f_B of B such that π ∘ f = f_B ∘ π?
accepted.context_brief: Invariant fibrations for birational maps of dynamical degree one

evidence.quote: Instead of assuming that the entropy of f is zero, one may now assume that λ1(f) = 1, i.e. that degH(f n) does not grow exponentially fast with n.
One may also ask, as in Question 3.1, whether the equality λ1(f) = 1 implies the existence of a non-trivial invariant fibration.

By “non-trivial meromorphic fibration”, I mean that 0 < dim(B) < dim(X) and π is a dominant rational map; and f permutes the fibers of π if there is a birational transformation fB of B such that π ◦ f = fB ◦ π.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a complex projective variety of dimension 3. If X admits a minimal automorphism f, meaning that every orbit of f is dense and hence the only f-invariant closed subsets are X and the empty set, must X be an abelian variety?

evidence.quote: A continuous transformation g of a compact metric space M is minimal if each of its orbits are dense; equivalently, the only g-invariant closed subsets are M and the empty set.
Question 3.3. Let X be a complex projective variety of dimension 3. Suppose that there is a minimal automorphism f on X. Is X an abelian variety ?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a complex projective K3 surface X with an automorphism f: X → X such that f has positive topological entropy and the Fatou set Fat(f) is nonempty, where Fat(f) is the f-invariant open set of points having a neighborhood on which the family of iterates (f^m)_{m∈Z} is normal in the sense of Montel?
accepted.context_brief: Positive-entropy automorphisms of projective K3 surfaces with Fatou set

evidence.quote: More precisely, define the Fatou set Fat(f) as follows: x ∈ X(C) is in the Fatou set if there is an open neighborhood V of x such that the sequence of iterates (f m)m∈Z forms a normal family on V, in the sense of Montel. This determines an f-invariant open subset Fat(f) ⊂ X(C) on which µf vanishes.
Question 3.4. Does there exist a complex projective K3 surface X with an automorphism f : X → X such that the topological entropy of f is positive and the Fatou set of f is not empty ?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a real projective K3 surface X_R with an automorphism f: X_R → X_R such that λ_1(f) > 1, the real locus X(R) is nonempty, and at least one of the following holds: (1) the topological entropy of f on X(R) equals the topological entropy of f on X(C); (2) the entropy of f on some connected component S of X(R) is zero; or (3) some connected component S of X(R) is contained in the Fatou set of f?
accepted.context_brief: Comparing real and complex dynamics on K3 surfaces

evidence.quote: Question 3.5. Does there exist a real projective K3 surface XR with an automorphism f : XR → XR such that λ1(f) > 1, X(R) is not empty, and one of the following propery occurs (1) the entropy of f on X(R) is equal to the entropy of f on X(C) ? (2) the entropy of f on some component S of X(R) vanishes ? (3) a connected component S of X(R) is contained in the Fatou set of f ?
